transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a customer order for 1800 cartons of the new 750-milliliter format due by Monday morning, and Line 6 is available for a Saturday shift. I understand the new format has had a dry fit on Line 6, but no production run has been authorized yet. That decision is mine to make. Before I can authorize anything, I need to go through our normal Saturday startup routine — I'll need quality, maintenance, and safety to each report and formally record their findings. I'd like to hear from each of you now so we can assess where things stand.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from my quality review. I completed the review of the new-format trial paperwork yesterday, and it specifies that the first production run requires a 30-minute first-article approval and 100% inspection of the first 200 cartons. However, I should note that the paperwork is still in quality's unfiled trial folder, so it hasn't been formally recorded yet. I'll make sure it gets filed and recorded as part of this startup review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report my maintenance findings. I checked the installed servo controller's latest firmware record this morning — I received it from the vendor — and it confirms that the new 750-milliliter format must run at exactly 90 cartons per minute or slower on Line 6. The format changeover also requires 2 hours of mechanical setup. I should note that the maintenance work order has not been opened yet, so this hasn't been formally recorded in our system.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to report my safety findings from yesterday's walkdown on Line 6. The new 750-milliliter format's guide adjustment requires two trained employees during setup, and a marked 1.5-meter exclusion zone must be maintained around the infeed. I documented this finding during the walkdown, but I want to flag that the Saturday startup board has not yet been updated with this information, so it hasn't been formally recorded there yet. I'll make sure it gets recorded as part of this startup review.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: File and formally record the first-article approval and 100% inspection of first 200 cartons requirement from the trial paperwork as part of this startup review.
Open the maintenance work order and formally record the 90 CPM maximum speed and 2-hour setup requirement for the 750-milliliter format on Line 6.
Update the Saturday startup board with the two-trained-employee setup requirement and 1.5-meter infeed exclusion zone finding.
Verify that two trained employees are assigned for setup before mechanical setup begins, as a post-meeting commitment.
Confirm the 2-hour mechanical setup is scheduled and completed before production begins.
